Warsaw Banks Disrupted as Protesters Blockade Branches Amid Political Dispute

Banks across several Polish cities are facing ongoing disruptions today as protesters blockaded branches and corporate offices in what officials describe as a politically motivated action targeting the financial sector. The demonstrations, which began early this morning in Warsaw, Kraków, and Gdańsk, have forced at least 40 branches of major banks such as PolBank Polska and Centralny Bank Ludowy to suspend in-person operations, according to the Polish Banking Association.

Eyewitnesses report that dozens of protesters have chained themselves to entryways and staged sit-ins inside lobbies, demanding policy changes related to recent government actions. “We are currently unable to access our premises or serve customers at several key locations,” said a spokesperson for PolBank Polska. “The safety of our staff is our highest priority, and we are monitoring the situation closely.”

Bank employees at affected sites have either been sent home or asked to work remotely where possible. “There’s a lot of uncertainty. We’re worried about how long this will last and whether our jobs are at risk,” said Marta Nowak, a teller at a branch near Warsaw’s city center.

Authorities are working to mediate the situation, but at press time, blockades remained in place. The Polish Banking Association warned that the continued occupation could have significant consequences for staff and operations if not resolved soon. “We urge all parties to remain calm and respect the rule of law,” said association president Andrzej Michalski. “Our members are committed to serving the public and ensuring the stability of the banking system.”
